action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"); Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - File search: Use Glob (NOT find or ls)
 - Content search: Use Grep (NOT grep or rg)
 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

  - Multiline matching: By default patterns match within single lines only. For cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`, use `multiline: true`

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

python3 -c "
import re, math

path = 'out/elbow_tube_x1_L48.gcode'
PIVOT = 48.0
OFF = 15.0  # PART_OFFSET_R

line_re = re.compile(r'^G0*1?\s.*')
r = c = z = b = 0.0
have_r=have_c=have_z=have_b=False
pts = []  # (x,y,z, extruding)
prev_e = None

with open(path) as f:
    for line in f:
        line=line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith(';'):
            continue
        if not line.startswith('G'):
            continue
        mY = re.search(r'Y(-?[\d.]+)', line)
        mX = re.search(r'X(-?[\d.]+)', line)
        mZ = re.search(r'Z(-?[\d.]+)', line)
        mB = re.search(r'B(-?[\d.]+)', line)
        mE = re.search(r'E(-?[\d.]+)', line)
        if mY: c = float(mY.group(1))
        if mX: r = float(mX.group(1))
        if mZ: z = float(mZ.group(1))
        if mB: b = float(mB.group(1))
        extruding = mE is not None
        # undo pivot compensation
        B = math.radians(b)
        r_tip = r - PIVOT*math.sin(B)
        z_tip = z + PIVOT*(1-math.cos(B))
        a = math.radians(c)
        x = r_tip*math.cos(a) - OFF
        y = r_tip*math.sin(a)
        pts.append((x,y,z_tip,extruding,b))

print('total points', len(pts))

# Look at points where b is between, say, 20 and 30 deg (mid-overhang), extruding
sel = [p for p in pts if p[3] and 20.0 <= p[4] <= 30.0]
print('points with b in [20,30] extruding:', len(sel))
if sel:
    xs = [p[0] for p in sel]
    ys = [p[1] for p in sel]
    zs = [p[2] for p in sel]
    print('x range', min(xs), max(xs))
    print('y range', min(ys), max(ys))
    print('z range', min(zs), max(zs))
"

21	resserrait", plateau parti en butee. Trace dans le G-code de septembre :
22	derniere ligne Y111600, soit 310 TOURS cumules.

26	constant et faire balayer C sur 360 deg -- tres elegant tant que la piece
27	est un pilier vertical, et c'est CE QUI CASSE des que la tete s'incline :
28	la section, elle, cesse d'etre centree sur l'axe (elle part a l'horizontale
29	avec la branche), mais le script continuait de lui faire faire un tour
30	complet par couche en reduisant son rayon machine. D'ou le col qui se
31	resserre en vrille.

34	Jamais de rotation continue, nulle part, y compris sur le pilier et sur la
35	premiere couche ou elle serait pourtant tentante (et "naturelle" pour un
36	plateau tournant). Deux raisons, dans cet ordre :
37	
38	  1. Un CHANGEMENT de regime en cours de piece est precisement ce qui a
39	     casse en septembre : la rotation continue tenait tant que la section
40	     restait centree, puis la geometrie cessait de le permettre sans que le
41	     mouvement change -- d'ou le goulot en vrille.

44	     vertical fixe, et R ne franchit jamais le centre. Un point (x,y) n'est
45	     atteignable que si le plateau l'amene dans ce plan, donc C = atan2(y,x)

47	     360 deg, point. Aucune oscillation de R ou de B n'atteint un point
48	     situe derriere l'axe.

58	donc dans la direction opposee : le surplomb s'etend vers +R, vers

74	
75	Usage : python scripts/gen_elbow_tube_gcode.py [sortie.gcode] [--speed N] [--pivot L] [--infill D] [--pattern P]
76	  --speed N : multiplie TOUTES les vitesses par N (defaut 1)
77	  --pivot L : distance pivot B -> pointe de buse, mm (defaut 0)

"""G-code AUTONOME : tube coude en surplomb, machine Apex 4 axes.

Ne depend de RIEN du projet (ni pipeline, ni core) : un seul fichier,
stdlib seule. Remplace scripts/gen_l_overhang_gcode.py, dont l'impression
du 1er septembre a rate -- voir "LE DEFAUT CORRIGE" ci-dessous.

PIECE : un tube ROND de diametre TUBE_DIAMETER.
  - branche verticale  : PILLAR_HEIGHT mm (axe du tube vertical)
  - coude              : l'axe du tube bascule de 90 deg (vertical ->
                         horizontal), la tete s'incline de 0 a 45 deg
  - branche horizontale: OVERHANG_LENGTH mm, en surplomb pur

SORTIE FIRMWARE : G00 Y<C> X<R> Z<Z> B<B> [E<e>] F<f>
  X = R, rayon plateau (mm) ; Y = C, rotation plateau (deg) ;
  Z = hauteur (mm) ; B = inclinaison tete (deg, 0 = buse vers le bas).

=============================================================================
LE DEFAUT CORRIGE (impression ratee du 1er septembre)
=============================================================================
Symptome rapporte : "une mini-bouteille dont le goulot se tordait et se
resserrait", plateau parti en butee. Trace dans le G-code de septembre :
derniere ligne Y111600, soit 310 TOURS cumules.

Cause : l'ancien script tracait la section du tube comme un cercle CENTRE
SUR L'AXE DE ROTATION (R=0). Tracer un cercle centre, c'est maintenir R
constant et faire balayer C sur 360 deg -- tres elegant tant que la piece
est un pilier vertical, et c'est CE QUI CASSE des que la tete s'incline :
la section, elle, cesse d'etre centree sur l'axe (elle part a l'horizontale
avec la branche), mais le script continuait de lui faire faire un tour
complet par couche en reduisant son rayon machine. D'ou le col qui se
resserre en vrille.

Correction : UN SEUL REGIME DE MOUVEMENT SUR TOUTE LA PIECE -- l'oscillation.
Jamais de rotation continue, nulle part, y compris sur le pilier et sur la
premiere couche ou elle serait pourtant tentante (et "naturelle" pour un
plateau tournant). Deux raisons, dans cet ordre :

  1. Un CHANGEMENT de regime en cours de piece est precisement ce qui a
     casse en septembre : la rotation continue tenait tant que la section
     restait centree, puis la geometrie cessait de le permettre sans que le
     mouvement change -- d'ou le goulot en vrille.
  2. La cinematique interdit l'oscillation sur une piece centree. La tete
     n'a que deux libertes de position (R et Z) : elle balaie un DEMI-PLAN
     vertical fixe, et R ne franchit jamais le centre. Un point (x,y) n'est
     atteignable que si le plateau l'amene dans ce plan, donc C = atan2(y,x)
     est IMPOSE par le point. Contour qui entoure l'axe => C parcourt
     360 deg, point. Aucune oscillation de R ou de B n'atteint un point
     situe derriere l'axe.

D'ou PART_OFFSET_R : on decale la piece pour que son contour n'entoure
jamais l'axe. C'est ce decalage, et lui seul, qui rend l'oscillation
possible.

=============================================================================
CONVENTION DE TETE (verifiee avec l'utilisateur, pas supposee)
=============================================================================
B > 0 penche la buse VERS LE CENTRE du plateau (vers -R). La matiere pousse
donc dans la direction opposee : le surplomb s'etend vers +R, vers
l'exterieur du plateau. Toute la geometrie ci-dessous en decoule.

=============================================================================
CE QUE CE SCRIPT NE PEUT PAS GARANTIR (a verifier avant de lancer)
=============================================================================
1. PIVOT DE LA TETE. Si l'axe de rotation B ne passe pas exactement par la
   pointe de la buse, incliner la tete DEPLACE la pointe, et il faut
   compenser. Regler PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM (0 = le firmware compense deja, ou
   le pivot est a la pointe). Se mesure en 30 s : jog B de 0 a 90 deg et
   regarder de combien la pointe se deplace.
2. SEMANTIQUE DE F. Le firmware voit Y (degres) comme un axe lineaire : la
   vitesse reelle de la buse depend donc du rayon. Ce script calcule F par
   segment pour tenir une vitesse MATIERE constante (voir _feed_for).
   Si votre firmware ignore les axes rotatifs dans son calcul de vitesse,
   mettre CONSTANT_FEED = True pour retrouver le comportement de septembre.

Usage : python scripts/gen_elbow_tube_gcode.py [sortie.gcode] [--speed N] [--pivot L] [--infill D] [--pattern P]
  --speed N : multiplie TOUTES les vitesses par N (defaut 1)
  --pivot L : distance pivot B -> pointe de buse, mm (defaut 0)
  --infill D : densite du remplissage, 0 a 1 (defaut 0.2 ; 0 = tube creux)
  --pattern P : gyroid (defaut) ou lines (zigzag alterne)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
import sys

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parametres piece
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TUBE_DIAMETER = 10.0        # diametre EXTERIEUR du tube, mm
PILLAR_HEIGHT = 15.0        # branche verticale (demande utilisateur), mm
OVERHANG_LENGTH = 30.0      # branche horizontale en surplomb (idem), mm
OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG = 45.0   # inclinaison de tete atteinte progressivement

# Rayon de courbure de l'axe du tube dans le coude, mm. Fixe la douceur du
# raccord : trop petit, le tube se pince a l'interieur du virage ; trop
# grand, le coude mange toute la hauteur disponible. TUBE_DIAMETER donne un
# coude franc mais sain (rayon interieur = TUBE_DIAMETER/2, jamais nul).
BEND_RADIUS = TUBE_DIAMETER

# Decalage de TOUTE la piece par rapport a l'axe de rotation du plateau, mm.
#
# CE PARAMETRE N'EST PAS COSMETIQUE : il conditionne le regime de mouvement.
# La tete n'a que deux libertes de position (R et Z), donc elle ne balaie
# qu'un DEMI-PLAN vertical fixe ; R ne franchit jamais le centre. Un point
# de la piece a (x,y) n'est atteignable que si le plateau l'amene dans ce
# plan, c'est-a-dire a C = atan2(y, x) : C est IMPOSE par le point, jamais
# libre. Si le contour entoure l'axe, atan2 parcourt 360 deg et le plateau
# DOIT faire un tour complet par couche -- aucune oscillation de R ou de B
# ne peut aller chercher un point situe derriere l'axe.
#
# Mesure (voir l'historique de mise au point) : contour du tube D10, le
# decalage minimal qui supprime tout tour complet est ~9 mm.
#   decalage  0 mm -> C balaie 353 deg (tour complet, piece sur l'axe)
#   decalage  5 mm -> C balaie 177 deg (le contour frole encore l'axe)
#   decalage 10 mm -> C balaie  60 deg -> OSCILLATION sur toute la piece
#   decalage 15 mm -> C balaie  39 deg
PART_OFFSET_R = 15.0

content.text: Je note un détail important dans le commentaire : le tube est décalé de `PART_OFFSET_R=15mm` par rapport à l'axe de rotation. Ça veut dire que quand C oscille dans le coude, chaque point de la section transversale du tube est à une DISTANCE et un ANGLE différent de l'axe machine — donc le point le plus proche de l'axe et le point le plus loin ne bougent pas de façon symétrique. Vérifions si c'est ça qui aplatit la section visuellement quand on relie les points dans l'ordre du G-code plutôt que dans l'ordre géométrique du contour.

124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	
126	LAYER_HEIGHT = 0.2

128	FILAMENT_DIAMETER = 1.75
129	NOZZLE_TEMP = 195

172	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	# Geometrie de la piece
174	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	#
176	# Repere piece : X = direction du surplomb (vers +R), Z = hauteur, Y
177	# lateral. L'axe de rotation du plateau est la droite X=Y=0.
178	#
179	# L'axe du tube ("spine") est parametre par une abscisse curviligne s :
180	#   - s in [0, PILLAR_HEIGHT]      : montee verticale sur l'axe machine
181	#   - coude                        : arc de cercle de rayon BEND_RADIUS,
182	#                                    centre a (BEND_RADIUS, 0, PILLAR_HEIGHT)
183	#   - puis                         : horizontale vers +X
184	#
185	# La tete, elle, s'incline de 0 a OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG : l'axe du tube tourne
186	# de 90 deg, la tete seulement de 45. Les deux ne sont PAS lies -- c'est
187	# exactement ce qui fait du surplomb un surplomb.

189	_BEND_CENTER = (BEND_RADIUS, PILLAR_HEIGHT)       # (x, z), l'axe Y passe par la
190	_BEND_ARC = 0.5 * math.pi * BEND_RADIUS
191	_HORIZONTAL_Z = PILLAR_HEIGHT + BEND_RADIUS       # hauteur de l'axe horizontal
192	# L'axe est prolonge de _TUBE_RADIUS au-dela de la longueur demandee : les
193	# plans de coupe sont inclines a 45 deg, donc le DERNIER plan qui coupe
194	# encore le tube laisse une calotte de matiere au-dela de lui. Sans cette
195	# rallonge, la branche est tronquee de _TUBE_RADIUS (mesure : portee 40 mm
196	# au lieu des 45 attendus) -- la piece finit plus courte que commandee.
197	_SPINE_TOTAL = PILLAR_HEIGHT + _BEND_ARC + OVERHANG_LENGTH + _TUBE_RADIUS
198	
199	
200	def spine_at(s: float) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
201	    """Point de l'axe du tube et sa tangente, a l'abscisse curviligne s.
202	
203	    Retourne (x, z, tx, tz) : position dans le plan (X,Z) et tangente
204	    unitaire. Y vaut toujours 0 (l'axe du tube reste dans le plan Y=0 ;
205	    c'est la SECTION qui s'etend en Y).
206	    """
207	    if s <= PILLAR_HEIGHT:
208	        return 0.0, s, 0.0, 1.0
209	    if s <= PILLAR_HEIGHT + _BEND_ARC:
210	        a = (s - PILLAR_HEIGHT) / BEND_RADIUS          # angle parcouru, rad
211	        cx, cz = _BEND_CENTER
212	        return (cx - BEND_RADIUS * math.cos(a),
213	                cz + BEND_RADIUS * math.sin(a),
214	                math.sin(a), math.cos(a))
215	    d = s - PILLAR_HEIGHT - _BEND_ARC
216	    return BEND_RADIUS + d, _HORIZONTAL_Z, 1.0, 0.0
217	
218	
219	def tube_point(s: float, phi: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
220	    """Point de la SURFACE du tube : section circulaire a l'abscisse s.
221	
222	    phi = 0 pointe vers l'exterieur du virage (dos du tube), phi = pi vers
223	    l'interieur. La section est un vrai cercle de rayon _TUBE_RADIUS dans le
224	    plan PERPENDICULAIRE a la tangente : c'est ce qui fait un tube ROND,
225	    et non le cylindre oblique ecrase que produisait l'ancien script.
226	    """
227	    x, z, tx, tz = spine_at(s)
228	    # normale dans le plan (X,Z), perpendiculaire a la tangente
229	    nx, nz = tz, -tx
230	    return (x + _TUBE_RADIUS * math.cos(phi) * nx,
231	            _TUBE_RADIUS * math.sin(phi),
232	            z + _TUBE_RADIUS * math.cos(phi) * nz)
233	
234	
235	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	# Champ de decoupe : ce qui definit les COUCHES
237	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
238	#
239	# Une couche = une surface de niveau du champ height_field ci-dessous. Le
240	# champ encode l'inclinaison progressive de la tete :
241	#
242	#   - sous le coude   : plans horizontaux      (B = 0)
243	#   - dans le coude   : plans pivotant autour d'une droite fixe, la tete
244	#                       passant de 0 a 45 deg  (eventail de plans)
245	#   - au-dela         : plans PARALLELES a 45 deg, qui tranchent la branche
246	#                       horizontale en ellipses (B = 45 constant)
247	#
248	# L'eventail pivote autour de la droite Y a (x=BEND_RADIUS, z=PILLAR_HEIGHT),
249	# c'est-a-dire l'axe meme du coude : c'est la seule position ou les plans ne
250	# se croisent jamais a l'interieur de la matiere (sans quoi deux couches se
251	# chevaucheraient).

253	_FAN_PIVOT = _BEND_CENTER                      # (x, z)
254	_BETA_MAX = math.radians(OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG)
255	
256	
257	def _fan_angle(x: float, z: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
258	    """Angle du point autour du pivot de l'eventail, et distance au pivot.
259	
260	    Reference : 0 rad = rayon pivot -> DEBUT du coude (direction -X depuis
261	    le pivot), croissant vers +Z puis +X. Sur l'axe du tube, l'angle vaut
262	    donc 0 a l'entree du coude et +90 deg a sa sortie ; il est NEGATIF dans
263	    le pilier. Se tromper de reference ici renvoie B=0 en plein coude (et
264	    le tube repart en vrille au lieu de basculer) -- c'est exactement le
265	    bug corrige apres mesure sur la premiere version de ce script.
266	    """
267	    px, pz = _FAN_PIVOT
268	    dx, dz = x - px, z - pz
269	    if dx == 0.0 and dz == 0.0:
270	        return 0.0, 0.0
271	    return math.atan2(dz, -dx), math.hypot(dx, dz)
272	
273	
274	def height_field(x: float, z: float) -> float:
275	    """Hauteur de depot en un point : la couche k est le niveau k*LAYER_HEIGHT.
276	
277	    Construit pour etre CONTINU et monotone le long du tube, condition pour
278	    que les couches s'empilent sans se croiser.
279	    """
280	    _px, pz = _FAN_PIVOT
281	    ang, rho = _fan_angle(x, z)
282	
283	    if ang <= 0.0:
284	        return z                                   # plans horizontaux
285	    if ang >= _BETA_MAX:
286	        # plans paralleles inclines de _BETA_MAX, mesures depuis le plan
287	        # limite de l'eventail (continuite exacte en ang == _BETA_MAX)
288	        return pz + _BETA_MAX * BEND_RADIUS + rho * math.sin(ang - _BETA_MAX)
289	    # eventail : hauteur = arc parcouru, normalise au rayon du coude pour
290	    # que l'epaisseur de couche vaille LAYER_HEIGHT sur l'AXE du tube
291	    return pz + ang * BEND_RADIUS
292	
293	
294	def head_angle_deg(x: float, z: float) -> float:
295	    """Inclinaison B de la tete en un point : 0 sous le coude, 45 au-dela."""
296	    ang, _rho = _fan_angle(x, z)
297	    return math.degrees(min(max(ang, 0.0), _BETA_MAX))
298	
299	
300	def _bracket_s(phi: float, target: float) -> float | None:
301	    """Trouve s tel que height_field(surface(s, phi)) == target (bissection).
302	
303	    Retourne None si le niveau ne coupe pas cette generatrice. Le champ est
304	    monotone le long de chaque generatrice (verifie par construction : la
305	    normale des couches garde une composante positive sur la tangente du
306	    tube partout, tant que l'inclinaison reste <= 45 deg), donc une simple
307	    bissection suffit -- pas besoin de solveur.
308	    """
309	    lo, hi = 0.0, _SPINE_TOTAL
310	
311	    def f(s: float) -> float:
312	        x, _y, z = tube_point(s, phi)
313	        return height_field(x, z) - target
314	
315	    flo, fhi = f(lo), f(hi)
316	    if flo > 0.0 or fhi < 0.0:
317	        return None
318	    for _ in range(60):
319	        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
320	        if f(mid) < 0.0:
321	            lo = mid
322	        else:
323	            hi = mid

PART_OFFSET_R = 15.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parametres procede
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LAYER_HEIGHT = 0.2
EXTRUSION_WIDTH = 0.4
FILAMENT_DIAMETER = 1.75
NOZZLE_TEMP = 195
# None = AUCUNE commande de plateau dans le fichier (ni M140, ni M190, ni
# extinction en fin) : le plateau n'est pas chauffe par ce G-code.
BED_TEMP = None

# False = la SEULE commande de temperature du fichier est M109 (chauffer
# la buse et attendre). Consequence : la buse RESTE CHAUDE apres
# l'impression, a eteindre a la main. True = ajoute M104 S0 en fin.
NOZZLE_OFF_AT_END = False

PRINT_SPEED = 25.0          # vitesse MATIERE visee, mm/s (vraie vitesse buse)
FIRST_LAYER_SPEED = 12.0    # idem, couches d'adherence
TRAVEL_SPEED = 60.0

SOLID_BASE_LAYER_COUNT = 3  # couches lentes a Z fixe (adherence plateau)

# Remplissage de l'interieur du tube, a chaque couche a partir de la 2e (la
# 1re est deja un disque plein). Fraction de la surface remplie : 0 = tube
# creux (contour seul), 1 = plein. L'ecart entre deux lignes vaut
# EXTRUSION_WIDTH / INFILL_DENSITY. Surcharge : --infill D
INFILL_DENSITY = 0.2
# "gyroid" (defaut) ou "lines" (zigzag alterne). Surcharge : --pattern P
INFILL_PATTERN = "gyroid"

# Compensation du pivot de tete : distance (mm) entre l'axe de rotation B
# et la pointe de la buse. 0 = pivot a la pointe, ou firmware qui compense
# deja (cas le plus courant). Voir l'avertissement en tete de fichier.
PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM = 0.0

# Repli si le firmware ne compte PAS les axes rotatifs dans sa vitesse.
CONSTANT_FEED = False
CONSTANT_FEED_VALUE = 1800.0   # mm/min, utilise seulement si CONSTANT_FEED

MAX_CHORD_MM = 0.6          # subdivision max entre deux points commandes

# Multiplicateur global de TOUTES les vitesses (impression, premiere couche,
# trajets a vide). Surcharge en ligne de commande : --speed 2
SPEED_FACTOR = 1.0

_TUBE_RADIUS = TUBE_DIAMETER / 2.0
_FILAMENT_AREA = math.pi * (FILAMENT_DIAMETER / 2.0) ** 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Geometrie de la piece
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Repere piece : X = direction du surplomb (vers +R), Z = hauteur, Y
# lateral. L'axe de rotation du plateau est la droite X=Y=0.
#
# L'axe du tube ("spine") est parametre par une abscisse curviligne s :
#   - s in [0, PILLAR_HEIGHT]      : montee verticale sur l'axe machine
#   - coude                        : arc de cercle de rayon BEND_RADIUS,
#                                    centre a (BEND_RADIUS, 0, PILLAR_HEIGHT)
#   - puis                         : horizontale vers +X
#
# La tete, elle, s'incline de 0 a OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG : l'axe du tube tourne
# de 90 deg, la tete seulement de 45. Les deux ne sont PAS lies -- c'est
# exactement ce qui fait du surplomb un surplomb.

_BEND_CENTER = (BEND_RADIUS, PILLAR_HEIGHT)       # (x, z), l'axe Y passe par la
_BEND_ARC = 0.5 * math.pi * BEND_RADIUS
_HORIZONTAL_Z = PILLAR_HEIGHT + BEND_RADIUS       # hauteur de l'axe horizontal
# L'axe est prolonge de _TUBE_RADIUS au-dela de la longueur demandee : les
# plans de coupe sont inclines a 45 deg, donc le DERNIER plan qui coupe
# encore le tube laisse une calotte de matiere au-dela de lui. Sans cette
# rallonge, la branche est tronquee de _TUBE_RADIUS (mesure : portee 40 mm
# au lieu des 45 attendus) -- la piece finit plus courte que commandee.
_SPINE_TOTAL = PILLAR_HEIGHT + _BEND_ARC + OVERHANG_LENGTH + _TUBE_RADIUS


def spine_at(s: float) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Point de l'axe du tube et sa tangente, a l'abscisse curviligne s.

    Retourne (x, z, tx, tz) : position dans le plan (X,Z) et tangente
    unitaire. Y vaut toujours 0 (l'axe du tube reste dans le plan Y=0 ;
    c'est la SECTION qui s'etend en Y).
    """
    if s <= PILLAR_HEIGHT:
        return 0.0, s, 0.0, 1.0
    if s <= PILLAR_HEIGHT + _BEND_ARC:
        a = (s - PILLAR_HEIGHT) / BEND_RADIUS          # angle parcouru, rad
        cx, cz = _BEND_CENTER
        return (cx - BEND_RADIUS * math.cos(a),
                cz + BEND_RADIUS * math.sin(a),
                math.sin(a), math.cos(a))
    d = s - PILLAR_HEIGHT - _BEND_ARC
    return BEND_RADIUS + d, _HORIZONTAL_Z, 1.0, 0.0


def tube_point(s: float, phi: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Point de la SURFACE du tube : section circulaire a l'abscisse s.

    phi = 0 pointe vers l'exterieur du virage (dos du tube), phi = pi vers
    l'interieur. La section est un vrai cercle de rayon _TUBE_RADIUS dans le
    plan PERPENDICULAIRE a la tangente : c'est ce qui fait un tube ROND,
    et non le cylindre oblique ecrase que produisait l'ancien script.
    """
    x, z, tx, tz = spine_at(s)
    # normale dans le plan (X,Z), perpendiculaire a la tangente
    nx, nz = tz, -tx
    return (x + _TUBE_RADIUS * math.cos(phi) * nx,
            _TUBE_RADIUS * math.sin(phi),
            z + _TUBE_RADIUS * math.cos(phi) * nz)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Champ de decoupe : ce qui definit les COUCHES
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Une couche = une surface de niveau du champ height_field ci-dessous. Le
# champ encode l'inclinaison progressive de la tete :
#
#   - sous le coude   : plans horizontaux      (B = 0)
#   - dans le coude   : plans pivotant autour d'une droite fixe, la tete
#                       passant de 0 a 45 deg  (eventail de plans)
#   - au-dela         : plans PARALLELES a 45 deg, qui tranchent la branche
#                       horizontale en ellipses (B = 45 constant)
#
# L'eventail pivote autour de la droite Y a (x=BEND_RADIUS, z=PILLAR_HEIGHT),
# c'est-a-dire l'axe meme du coude : c'est la seule position ou les plans ne
# se croisent jamais a l'interieur de la matiere (sans quoi deux couches se
# chevaucheraient).

_FAN_PIVOT = _BEND_CENTER                      # (x, z)
_BETA_MAX = math.radians(OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG)


def _fan_angle(x: float, z: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Angle du point autour du pivot de l'eventail, et distance au pivot.

    Reference : 0 rad = rayon pivot -> DEBUT du coude (direction -X depuis
    le pivot), croissant vers +Z puis +X. Sur l'axe du tube, l'angle vaut
    donc 0 a l'entree du coude et +90 deg a sa sortie ; il est NEGATIF dans
    le pilier. Se tromper de reference ici renvoie B=0 en plein coude (et
    le tube repart en vrille au lieu de basculer) -- c'est exactement le
    bug corrige apres mesure sur la premiere version de ce script.
    """
    px, pz = _FAN_PIVOT
    dx, dz = x - px, z - pz
    if dx == 0.0 and dz == 0.0:
        return 0.0, 0.0
    return math.atan2(dz, -dx), math.hypot(dx, dz)


def height_field(x: float, z: float) -> float:
    """Hauteur de depot en un point : la couche k est le niveau k*LAYER_HEIGHT.

    Construit pour etre CONTINU et monotone le long du tube, condition pour
    que les couches s'empilent sans se croiser.
    """
    _px, pz = _FAN_PIVOT
    ang, rho = _fan_angle(x, z)

    if ang <= 0.0:
        return z                                   # plans horizontaux
    if ang >= _BETA_MAX:
        # plans paralleles inclines de _BETA_MAX, mesures depuis le plan
        # limite de l'eventail (continuite exacte en ang == _BETA_MAX)
        return pz + _BETA_MAX * BEND_RADIUS + rho * math.sin(ang - _BETA_MAX)
    # eventail : hauteur = arc parcouru, normalise au rayon du coude pour
    # que l'epaisseur de couche vaille LAYER_HEIGHT sur l'AXE du tube
    return pz + ang * BEND_RADIUS


def head_angle_deg(x: float, z: float) -> float:
    """Inclinaison B de la tete en un point : 0 sous le coude, 45 au-dela."""
    ang, _rho = _fan_angle(x, z)
    return math.degrees(min(max(ang, 0.0), _BETA_MAX))


def _bracket_s(phi: float, target: float) -> float | None:
    """Trouve s tel que height_field(surface(s, phi)) == target (bissection).

    Retourne None si le niveau ne coupe pas cette generatrice. Le champ est
    monotone le long de chaque generatrice (verifie par construction : la
    normale des couches garde une composante positive sur la tangente du
    tube partout, tant que l'inclinaison reste <= 45 deg), donc une simple
    bissection suffit -- pas besoin de solveur.
    """
    lo, hi = 0.0, _SPINE_TOTAL

    def f(s: float) -> float:
        x, _y, z = tube_point(s, phi)
        return height_field(x, z) - target

    flo, fhi = f(lo), f(hi)
    if flo > 0.0 or fhi < 0.0:
        return None
    for _ in range(60):
        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
        if f(mid) < 0.0:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid
    return 0.5 * (lo + hi)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cinematique machine
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def to_machine(x: float, y: float, z: float, b_deg: float,
               prev_c: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """(x, y, z) piece + inclinaison -> (R, C, Z) machine.

    C est ramene au plus proche de prev_c : sans ce recalage, un contour qui
    traverse +-180 deg ferait faire au plateau un tour complet en arriere.
    C'est aussi ce qui rend l'OSCILLATION lisible dans le fichier : C reste
    au voisinage de sa valeur precedente au lieu de sauter.
    """
    # Decalage applique ICI et nulle part ailleurs : toute la geometrie de
    # la piece est decrite dans un repere centre sur l'axe du tube, et ne
    # connait pas le plateau. Un seul endroit ou le decalage existe = aucun
    # risque qu'une partie du code l'applique et une autre l'oublie.
    x = x + PART_OFFSET_R

    r = math.hypot(x, y)
    c = prev_c if r < 1e-9 else math.degrees(math.atan2(y, x))
    c = _nearest_angle(c, prev_c)

    if PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM:
        # Le firmware positionne le PIVOT, pas la pointe. Calibre a B=0, la
        # commande P coincide avec la pointe ; incline de B (vers -R), la
        # pointe arrive en :
        #     pointe = P + (-L sin B, +L (1 - cos B))      [en (R, Z)]
        # c'est-a-dire vers le centre ET plus haut -- symptome observe en
        # impression : chaque couche s'ecarte du tube a l'oppose du bras.
        # Pour poser la pointe en T, il faut donc commander
        #     P = T + (+L sin B, -L (1 - cos B)).
        # (Premiere version : signe de Z inverse, qui doublait la montee au
        # lieu de l'annuler. Verifie par simulation directe, voir historique.)
        b = math.radians(b_deg)
        r += PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM * math.sin(b)
        z -= PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM * (1.0 - math.cos(b))
    return r, c, z


def _nearest_angle(target: float, ref: float) -> float:
    while target - ref > 180.0:
        target -= 360.0

def _section_points(level: float) -> list[tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Contour ferme d'une couche : intersection du niveau avec le tube.

    Pour chaque generatrice phi du tube, on cherche l'abscisse s ou le champ
    atteint le niveau demande. C'est ce qui donne de VRAIES ellipses dans la
    branche horizontale (plan a 45 deg coupant un tube rond), la ou l'ancien
    script dessinait un cercle dans le plan incline -- donc un tube ecrase.
    """
    n = max(48, int(math.ceil(2.0 * math.pi * _TUBE_RADIUS / MAX_CHORD_MM)))
    pts: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = []
    for i in range(n + 1):                      # +1 : referme le contour
        phi = 2.0 * math.pi * (i % n) / n
        s = _bracket_s(phi, level)
        if s is None:
            return []
        pts.append(tube_point(s, phi))
    return pts


def _rotate_contour_start(pts, near):
    """Fait pivoter un contour FERME pour qu'il commence au point le plus
    proche de `near`, au lieu de toujours repartir de phi=0.

    Sans ca, chaque contour recommence au meme point de reference alors que
    le remplissage de la couche precedente finit n'importe ou sur le disque
    interieur -- mesure sur elbow_tube_x1.gcode : un trajet a vide de 5 a
    12 mm entre quasiment CHAQUE couche, jamais visible comme un defaut
    d'extrusion (ce sont de vrais trajets a vide, sans E) mais dessine en
    trait plein par tout visualiseur qui ne distingue pas extrusion et
    trajet a vide -- c'est le "bec plat" observe en rendu externe.

    `pts` est une boucle fermee (pts[0] == pts[-1]) : n'importe quel indice
    peut servir de nouveau depart sans changer la forme du contour.
    """
    if near is None or len(pts) < 3:
        return pts
    body = pts[:-1]                        # sans le point de fermeture duplique
    best_i = min(range(len(body)), key=lambda i: math.dist(body[i], near))
    rotated = body[best_i:] + body[:best_i]
    rotated.append(rotated[0])              # referme la boucle au nouveau depart
    return rotated


def _emit_section(g: GCode, pts: list[tuple[float, float, float]],
                  speed: float, first_point_travel: bool) -> None:
    """Trace un contour ferme, en subdivisant pour rester fidele en (R,C)."""
    if first_point_travel:
        x, y, z = pts[0]
        b = head_angle_deg(x, z)
        g.go(x, y, z + 1.0, b, TRAVEL_SPEED, extrude=False)
        g.go(x, y, z, b, TRAVEL_SPEED, extrude=False)

    for i in range(1, len(pts)):
        x0, y0, z0 = pts[i - 1]
        x1, y1, z1 = pts[i]
        seg = math.dist((x0, y0, z0), (x1, y1, z1))
        steps = max(1, int(math.ceil(seg / MAX_CHORD_MM)))
        for k in range(1, steps + 1):
            t = k / steps
            x, y, z = (x0 + (x1 - x0) * t, y0 + (y1 - y0) * t,
                       z0 + (z1 - z0) * t)
            g.go(x, y, z, head_angle_deg(x, z), speed, extrude=True,
                 layer_thickness=_local_thickness(x, z))


def _emit_base_disc(g: GCode, level: float) -> None:
    """Premiere couche : disque plein, en VA-ET-VIENT (jamais une spirale).

    Une spirale d'Archimede centree serait le mouvement le plus naturel
    d'un plateau tournant -- et c'est precisement ce qu'on s'interdit ici :
    elle impose une rotation CONTINUE (12 tours mesures pour ce seul
    disque), alors que toute la piece doit rester en oscillation. Un
    balayage en va-et-vient parallele a Y garde C dans la meme plage etroite
    que les couches suivantes.

    ORDRE : contour D'ABORD, remplissage ensuite -- exception assumee a la
    regle "interieur vers exterieur" de CLAUDE.md, limitee a cette couche
    (la seule de la piece qui ait un remplissage). Pour une premiere couche :
      - le contour, pose sur un plateau propre, fixe le diametre du tube
        dont toute la paroi repose ensuite sur lui ;
      - chaque ligne de remplissage vient buter contre un cordon deja
        colle, au lieu d'avoir des extremites libres qui se relevent.
    """
    g.comment("couche 1 : contour puis disque plein (va-et-vient), B=0")
    pts = [(_TUBE_RADIUS * math.cos(2.0 * math.pi * i / 96),
            _TUBE_RADIUS * math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * i / 96), level)
           for i in range(97)]
    _emit_section(g, pts, FIRST_LAYER_SPEED, first_point_travel=True)

    n = max(2, int(math.ceil(2.0 * _TUBE_RADIUS / EXTRUSION_WIDTH)))
    first = True
    for i in range(n + 1):
        x = -_TUBE_RADIUS + 2.0 * _TUBE_RADIUS * i / n
        half = math.sqrt(max(0.0, _TUBE_RADIUS ** 2 - x * x))
        if half < 1e-6:
            continue
        y0, y1 = (-half, half) if i % 2 == 0 else (half, -half)
        # rejoint le debut de la ligne a vide, puis la trace en extrudant
        g.go(x, y0, level, 0.0, TRAVEL_SPEED, extrude=False)
        _emit_span(g, x, y0, x, y1, level, FIRST_LAYER_SPEED, first)
        first = False


def _emit_span(g: GCode, x0: float, y0: float, x1: float, y1: float,
               z: float, speed: float, _first: bool) -> None:
    """Un segment droit, subdivise pour rester fidele une fois en (R, C)."""
    seg = math.hypot(x1 - x0, y1 - y0)
    steps = max(1, int(math.ceil(seg / MAX_CHORD_MM)))
    for k in range(1, steps + 1):
        t = k / steps
        g.go(x0 + (x1 - x0) * t, y0 + (y1 - y0) * t, z, 0.0, speed,
             extrude=True)


def build() -> GCode:
    g = GCode()
    total_layers = int(math.floor(_max_field_level() / LAYER_HEIGHT))

    g.comment("=== tube coude en surplomb - gen_elbow_tube_gcode.py ===")
    g.comment("G00 Y<C> X<R> Z<Z> B<B> F  |  B>0 = buse penchee vers -R")
    g.comment(f"tube rond D{TUBE_DIAMETER} mm, pilier {PILLAR_HEIGHT} mm, "
              f"surplomb {OVERHANG_LENGTH} mm a {OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG} deg")
    g.comment(f"coude R{BEND_RADIUS} mm, couche {LAYER_HEIGHT} mm, "
              f"cordon {EXTRUSION_WIDTH} mm")
    g.comment(f"remplissage : {INFILL_PATTERN} {INFILL_DENSITY * 100:g} %"
              + ("  (tube creux)" if INFILL_DENSITY <= 0 else ""))
    g.comment(f"pivot B -> pointe : {PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM:g} mm"
              + ("  (AUCUNE compensation)" if not PIVOT_ABOVE_TIP_MM else ""))
    g.comment(f"vitesse x{SPEED_FACTOR:g} : impression "
              f"{PRINT_SPEED * SPEED_FACTOR:g} mm/s, couche 1 "
              f"{FIRST_LAYER_SPEED * SPEED_FACTOR:g} mm/s, vide "
              f"{TRAVEL_SPEED * SPEED_FACTOR:g} mm/s")
    g.raw()
    g.raw("G21")
    g.raw("G90")
    g.raw("M82")
    g.raw("G92 E0")
    if BED_TEMP is not None:
        g.raw(f"M140 S{BED_TEMP}")
    g.raw(f"M109 S{NOZZLE_TEMP}")
    if BED_TEMP is not None:
        g.raw(f"M190 S{BED_TEMP}")
    g.raw("G00 B0.0000 F1200")
    g.raw("G00 Y0.0000 X0.0000 Z5.0000 F1200")
    g.raw()

    phase = None
    for k in range(1, total_layers + 1):
        level = k * LAYER_HEIGHT
        if k == 1:
            _emit_base_disc(g, level)
            continue

        pts = _section_points(level)
        if not pts:
            break

        b_here = max(head_angle_deg(x, z) for x, _y, z in pts)
        new_phase = ("pilier" if b_here <= 1e-6 else
                     "coude" if b_here < OVERHANG_ANGLE_DEG - 1e-6 else
                     "surplomb")
        if new_phase != phase:
            phase = new_phase
            g.raw()
            if phase == "pilier":
                g.comment("--- pilier : B=0, R et C oscillent ---")
            elif phase == "coude":
                g.comment("--- coude : B monte vers 45 deg, R et C oscillent ---")
            else:
                g.comment("--- surplomb : B=45 constant, R et C oscillent ---")

        speed = FIRST_LAYER_SPEED if k <= SOLID_BASE_LAYER_COUNT else PRINT_SPEED
        infill = _infill_paths(level, k)
        # Avec remplissage, la couche ne finit plus a son point de depart :
        # il faut rejoindre le debut du contour par un trajet a vide. Sans
        # remplissage, on garde la continuite helicoidale d'origine.
        if infill:
            pts = _rotate_contour_start(pts, g.pos)
        _emit_section(g, pts, speed,
                      first_point_travel=(k == 2 or bool(infill)))
        _emit_infill(g, infill, speed)

    g.raw()
    g.comment("fin")
    # Degagement : remonter D'ABORD, redresser la tete ENSUITE. Avec un pivot
    # au-dessus de la pointe, redresser B en place fait decrire a la pointe
    # un arc de L*sin(B) vers l'exterieur et L*(1-cos B) vers le bas (32 mm
    # et 13 mm pour L=45), au ras de la piece juste imprimee. Monter tout
    # droit en gardant B eloigne la pointe du cote non encore imprime (la
    # derniere couche est la plus haute du champ), sans rien croiser.
    g.raw(f"G00 Z{_HORIZONTAL_Z + 30.0:.4f} F1200")
    g.raw("G00 B0.0000 F1200")
    if NOZZLE_OFF_AT_END:
        g.raw("M104 S0")
    if BED_TEMP is not None:
        g.raw("M140 S0")
    g.raw("M84")
    return g


def _max_field_level() -> float:
    """Niveau de champ le plus eleve atteint par la piece.

    C'est le NIVEAU (au sens de height_field), pas la hauteur Z : au bout de
    la branche horizontale le tube n'est qu'a z=25 alors que le champ y vaut
    ~51, les plans etant inclines a 45 deg. Confondre les deux tronque la
    piece avant meme le coude -- mesure sur la premiere version : 125
    couches au lieu de 256, aucun surplomb genere.

    Balaye la surface entiere (pas seulement l'axe) : le maximum est atteint
    sur une generatrice, jamais au centre.
    """
    best = 0.0
    for i in range(400):
        s = _SPINE_TOTAL * i / 399.0
        for j in range(72):
            x, _y, z = tube_point(s, 2.0 * math.pi * j / 72.0)
            best = max(best, height_field(x, z))
    return best

r = c = z = b = 0.0

content.text:
Voilà le bug, confirmé par lecture : la ligne 919 `G00 Z{...}` ne fixe QUE Z. Elle omet complètement **Y (C)** et **X (R)** — donc pour un firmware qui n'accepte pas de paramètres implicites conservés, ou pour n'importe quel visualiseur qui interprète l'absence de X/Y comme "reste à la dernière valeur commandée", la position R,C de fin est celle du tout dernier point de la dernière couche extrudée — c'est-à-dire une position quelconque du contour, pas alignée avec la pièce.

Et surtout, la ligne 920 `G00 B0.0000` remet la buse à la verticale, mais **au R,C où elle se trouvait déjà** (puisque ni R ni C ne sont redonnés) — donc juste après avoir monté en Z, la tête se redresse à un endroit du plateau qui n'a aucun rapport visuel avec l'axe du tube. Sur le rendu, ça affiche la buse penchée n'importe comment juste avant de se redresser, ou dans un état intermédiaire si l'animation s'arrête pile à cette transition.

Le vrai souci : ce n'est **pas** un problème de rendu, c'est que le G-code de fin ne spécifie jamais explicitement où se trouve la tête en X/Y — ce qui est fragile. Je corrige en répétant explicitement R et C à ces deux lignes finales, pour que la fin de trajectoire soit toujours déterministe.
